name: Ice Age Trail 50K
description: 25 weeks, Nov 16, 2026 to the race on May 8, 2027. Long-run times assume 12:00 a mile.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Base
phases.summary: Build the habit, set your baselines, lift three times a week. The long run grows to 10 miles.

phases.name: Phase 2 · Build
phases.summary: Tuesday hills, Wednesday runs, more food. Long runs reach 3 hours; Saturday runs start.

phases.name: Phase 3 · Peak
phases.summary: Back-to-back weekends. Biggest runs Apr 11 and 18. The deficit ends Mar 28.

phases.name: Taper and race
phases.summary: Miles drop, keep the strides. Race Saturday, May 8.

A.name: Strength A
notes: Stop every set with 2–3 reps in reserve. Start single-side work on your weaker side and match the reps. End the set when your form changes.
Add pogo hops and low box jumps (Phase 2 on) only if your back allows.

notes: Stop every set with 2–3 reps in reserve. Start single-side work on your weaker side and match the reps. End the set when your form changes.

notes: Stop every set with 2–3 reps in reserve. Start single-side work on your weaker side and match the reps. End the set when your form changes.

routine.name: Spine routine
steps: Side-rib breathing into your left ribs: 10 breaths, 5 s in, 7 s out
Child's pose side reach: 3 × 30 s each way, one extra to the right
Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch: 45 s each side

effort.meaning: Full sentences, about 120–140 bpm. Walk hills that break the talk test.
4–6 × 20 s, fast but relaxed, full recovery.
60–90 s uphill at 7 out of 10. Walk back down.
10–15 min blocks, comfortably hard. 3 min easy between.
Easy all the way. Power-hike the climbs.

notes.title: When to change the plan
bullets: Weight over 0.5 lb a week behind for two weeks: cut 150 kcal. Losing over 2 lb a week: add 200.
Back score 2 over baseline for 48 hours: cut next week’s volume 25%.
Lifts down 10%, or resting heart rate up 7 beats: eat at maintenance and add a rest day.
Low libido, low mood or repeated illness: stop the deficit and tell your doctor.
Leg numbness or weakness, night pain, chest pain or pinpoint bone pain: stop and get seen.

notes.title: This month
bullets: Lift before you run. Strength is the priority while mileage is low.
Every run is easy: full sentences. Walk hills that break the talk test.
Two rest days a week: Monday and Thursday. The long run is on Sunday.
Weigh every morning, compare weekly averages. Expect about 1.4 lb a week.
Weigh and log your food for the first four weeks.

notes.title: This month
bullets: Keep lifting before you run.
Wednesday adds a short easy run from Dec 16.
Long runs over 90 minutes (Dec 20 on): take 30 g of carbs an hour.
The week of Dec 7 is a down week. Do not add miles.
On snow or ice, wear traction devices and run by time, not miles.

notes.title: This month
bullets: Through Jan 10, keep the December pattern. From Jan 11, run before you lift.
Tuesday hills: hard but controlled, 7 out of 10. Walk back down.
Wednesday becomes an easy run plus a short Strength C. Rest days stay Monday and Thursday.
Food goes up to about 3,000 kcal a day on Jan 11. Eat it.
Take 30 g of carbs an hour on every long run.
Register for the race and check its cutoff time.

notes.title: This month
bullets: The week of Feb 1 is a down week: Wednesday is bike and Strength C, no run.
Long runs build to 3:00 on Feb 28.
From Feb 14: 40 g of carbs an hour, and Saturday adds an easy run.
Add pogo hops and low box jumps to Strength A if your back allows.
Treadmill hills at 4–8% are fine. Keep treadmill long runs under 90 minutes.
Feb 28: first 3-hour long run. Carry two flasks and your own gels.
Film yourself running from behind. Compare left and right side-plank times.
Confirm your race entry and the cutoff time.

notes.title: This month
bullets: The week of Mar 1 is a down week. Peak starts Mar 8.
Sunday long runs pass 3 hours. Keep Saturday’s run truly easy: it sets up Sunday.
Run every long run in the Southern Kettle Moraine. Include the Nordic loop.
Take 50 g of carbs an hour. Practice aid-station food. Do a sweat test.
The deficit ends Mar 28. If you are above 203 lb, do not extend it.
Strength drops to two sets. Never lift to soreness.
Repeat your bloodwork this month.

notes.title: This month
bullets: Eat at maintenance all month. No deficit.
Apr 11 is 22 miles. Apr 18 is 24 miles, the longest run.
Rehearse race day on Apr 18: breakfast, vest, shoes, fueling.
Taper starts Apr 19. Miles drop. Keep the strides.
One light strength session a week, on Tuesday, at 80% of your usual weights.

notes.title: This month
bullets: No strength work in race week.
Thursday and Friday: carb load. Expect the scale to jump 3–4 lb.
Nothing new on race day: shoes, vest, socks and food have all done a long run.
After the race: two easy weeks at maintenance.
Then a 500 kcal deficit for about seven weeks reaches 10% around mid-July.

notes.title: Food timing
bullets: Four meals a day, 45–55 g of protein each.
30–60 g of carbs one to two hours before any run over an hour. Never run Tuesday’s session or the long run fasted.
On runs over 90 minutes, take carbs every hour. They count toward the day.
Eat a meal with 40 g or more of protein within two hours after training.

notes.title: Race day plan
bullets: Eat 90–135 g of carbs two to three hours before the start.
Every hour: about 50 g carbs, 15–25 oz fluid, 250–450 mg sodium. Start in the first 30 minutes.
The first hour should feel too easy. Keep your heart rate under about 140 through the hilly first section.
Hike every climb from the first mile.
Save caffeine for the second half.
The race ends with two loops of the runnable Nordic Trail. Use the legs you saved.
Nine aid stations are listed, seven with food. Carry your own gels anyway.
Confirm your 50K start time on the race website.
Stop for new leg numbness or weakness, chest pain, or breathlessness out of proportion to the effort.

days.label: Recover: walk, eat and sleep. No running this week.
